title: Sneaky E
rule: A vowel, then one consonant, then an e at the end. The e is silent and sneaky: it makes the vowel say its name.
trickText: Look at the end of the word. Vowel, consonant, e? Put a macron over the vowel and cross out the e. No sneaky e? A vowel with a consonant after it is short, so it gets a breve.
say: Today's case is the sneaky e. When a word ends with a vowel, a consonant, and an e, the e is silent. It sneaks in and makes the first vowel say its name. Put a macron on the vowel and cross out the e.

example.say: Look at cake. The e at the end is sneaky. It makes the a say its name. So I put a macron on the a, and I cross out the e.

activities.instruction: Code each word. Sneaky e words get a macron and a crossed out e. Short vowels get a breve.
Listen to the word. Does it have a sneaky e, or a short vowel?

categories.label: Sneaky e
categories.why: It ends with a vowel, a consonant, and an e. The e is silent and the vowel says its name.

categories.label: Short vowel
categories.why: There is no sneaky e at the end, so the vowel is short.
